data.name: Ax
data.gender_notes: Ax is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'axon', meaning 'sharp edge' or 'axe'. In ancient Greece, the god Apollo was associated with the axe, symbolizing purification and protection. In the New Testament, the Apostle Paul refers to himself as a 'sharp sword of the Spirit' (Ephesians 6:17). The name Ax carries the meaning “Secure, protected” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ax usually hope their child will grow to embody secure, protected and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of protection and divine guidance.
data.etymology: Ax belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Secure, protected.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ax total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Ax' has a unique cultural significance as it originated from the Greek word 'axon', which was symbolically linked to the god Apollo's axe. This association represented purification and protection, instilling a sense of strength and power. Over time, the name came to be associated with the innovative, inventive, and pioneering spirit, as the ax was a tool used for cutting through tough materials, clearing new paths, and creating new opportunities.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian faith, the name 'Ax' takes on a deeper meaning, as it symbolizes the sharp sword of the Spirit wielded by the Apostle Paul in Ephesians 6:17. This powerful metaphor emphasizes the importance of the Word of God, acting as a weapon against spiritual forces of evil, and the essential role of spiritual discernment in navigating the complexities of life. The name Ax can serve as a constant reminder of the power and protection found in the power of the Word and the guidance of the Holy Spirit.
